items.title: myDBR 7.7 brings web reporting to PostgreSQL
items.summary: Helsinki, Finland, 2026-10-28 - myDBR.com announced PostgreSQL support in myDBR, its web-based reporting platform for SQL databases. PostgreSQL 12 or later can now hold both myDBR's own objects and the reports, alongside the MySQL, MariaDB and Microsoft SQL Server support that myDBR already has.What is myDBR?myDBR turns SQL into a finished reporting portal. A developer writes the report logic in the database. myDBR supplies the web interface: parameter forms, tables, charts, maps, drill-downs, scheduling, user management and export to Excel, PDF and CSV. Users need only a browser, and there is no separate report designer or proprietary query language to learn. If you can write a query, you can publish a report.What PostgreSQL support coversReports as PL/pgSQL functions. A report is a function that returns one cursor per result set. Titles, charts, tables, tabs and maps are each a result set, so one function can build a full report page.Simple installation. The web installer creates the role and database, and runs the creation script as a single transaction, so a failure leaves nothing half installed. myDBR can live in its own schema next to your data, which suits PostgreSQL's one-database-per-connection model.Row-level security. myDBR can pass the logged-in user to PostgreSQL, or run each report as that user's database role. The database itself then decides which rows a user sees, and a copied or modified report cannot show more than the user is allowed to see.Report timeouts and a running-reports view. Administrators can set global or per-report limits using statement_timeout and lock_timeout. They can also see the reports running now and cancel them.Developer tools. The SQL Editor, query plan viewer (EXPLAIN), data browser, query builder, synchronization between servers, Git version control and the AI report assistant all work with PostgreSQL.RequirementsPostgreSQL 12 or later (14 or later recommended), PHP 8.0 or later with the pgsql extension, and the citext contrib extension.AvailabilityPostgreSQL support is included in myDBR 7.7. Documentation, including an installation guide and a PL/pgSQL report tutorial, is available at https://www.mydbr.com/doc. To learn more and download a trial, visit the https://www.mydbr.com.About myDBRmyDBR is developed by myDBR.com. It has been used for database reporting since 2004 and is used by organizations of all sizes to publish reports from their SQL databases to the web.

items.title: ReinDB: read-only performance monitoring for PostgreSQL, first database free
items.summary: Bandlei has released ReinDB, read-only performance monitoring for PostgreSQL, self-managed or on Amazon RDS and Aurora.ReinDB learns what normal looks like for each database and statement, hour by hour, using pg_stat_statements, and flags what drifts from it, ranked by the extra database time each change costs. Each flag shows the evidence, including plan history, and a fix script your DBA can test, with an undo for each step.ReinDB installs nothing in your database and needs one read-only login. It runs hosted, onsite on Linux or Windows, or in your own AWS or Google Cloud account. MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle are also supported.The first database is free for one person, with no time limit and no card. A free 109-page guide, Rein In Your Database, covers the tuning method behind it.More at reindb.com.

items.title: Autobase 2.12 released
items.summary: We are pleased to announce the release of Autobase  2.12!HighlightsBuilt-in Monitoring DashboardsAutobase isn't intended to replace your monitoring system. Instead, we've integrated with Netdata, which we consider one of the best solutions for real-time infrastructure monitoring.Autobase Platform now includes built-in dashboards powered by the Netdata agent, providing convenient access to key metrics for:System — CPU, memory, disk, and network performancePostgreSQL — database health and performancePgBouncer — connection pooling metricsTables and Indexes — statistics and performance insightsExplore the dashboards in our live demo sandbox: https://demo.autobase.techMulti-AZ DeploymentWhen provisioning PostgreSQL clusters on AWS, GCP, and Azure, Autobase now distributes nodes across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) by default.This improves cluster resilience by reducing the impact of a single Availability Zone failure.Implementation details:AWS — PR #1732GCP — PR #1738Azure — PR #1740External Secrets Provider: AWS Secrets ManagerWe've introduced a new secrets role with support for AWS Secrets Manager.This integration enables Autobase to export and store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager, providing an option for centralized secrets management.Security EnhancementsAutobase 2.12 includes important security improvements across the platform and automation engine:Redacted sensitive credentials and secrets from API request and service logs.Replaced PGPASSWORD environment variables with secure password files.Prevented sensitive pgBackRest configuration details from appearing in logs.Enforced IMDSv2 for AWS EC2 instances.Added EBS encryption and AWS KMS key support.Reliability ImprovementsThis release also improves the safety and reliability of cluster management, backup, and restore operations:Preserved WAL archiving and prevented unintended replica promotion during restore operations.Fixed a race condition when creating pgBackRest stanzas on shared POSIX repositories.Fixed cluster management operations when etcd/DCS runs on dedicated hosts.Added persistent backup storage identifiers for more reliable cluster management.SSH Jump Host SupportAdded support for connecting to PostgreSQL servers through SSH jump hosts (bastion hosts).This enables Autobase to manage clusters in private networks without requiring direct SSH access to database servers.Release notesSee the full details in the release notes.About AutobaseAutobase is an Internal Database Platform for PostgreSQL, bringing the managed database experience of DBaaS into your own infrastructure.Deploy, operate, and scale production-ready, highly available PostgreSQL clusters across bare metal, virtual machines, on-premises infrastructure, and supported cloud providers.Website: https://autobase.tech
